title: Effect of tamarind seed polysaccharide on ice cream quality.
abstract: Ice recrystallization is a key factor limiting the storage stability of ice cream. Although tamarind seed polysaccharide (TSP) is recognized for its thickening and ice recrystallization inhibition (IRI) capabilities, its specific mechanism of action in frozen dairy systems remains underexplored. This study aimed to elucidate the stabilizing mechanism of TSP (0%, 0.2%, and 0.5% w/w) in ice cream formulations. Rheological analysis revealed that TSP significantly modified the flow properties of the mixes. The consistency coefficient (K) increased from 0.4451 to 1.1593 Pa·s These findings demonstrate that TSP is a potent cryostabilizer that optimizes the microstructural integrity and textural quality of ice cream. This research provides a robust theoretical foundation for utilizing TSP as a functional ingredient in the frozen dessert industry. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
